Minea, V. (2012). Using industrial heat pumps in sawmills for lumber drying. IEA Heat Pump Centre Newsletter No. 1/2012 (Hydro-Quebec Research Institute, Laboratoire des technologies de l'energie). 11 pp. Venue and issue taken from the PDF metadata title "Minea, Sawmills, NL 1, 2012"; not printed on the article.

Locators are the printed article page numbers 1-11 (= PDF pages). Canadian (Quebec) data, measured. Main file: three examples of kiln_lumber-heat-pump - the 13 m3 laboratory hardwood dryer (5.6 kW low-temperature heat pump), the hybrid test 5H (heat pump plus natural-gas steam back-up) with whole-dryer energy per t water extracted, and the 354 m3 industrial softwood dryer with two 65 kW high-temperature heat pumps (COP 3-4.6, SMER-derived electricity per t water, 14.75 USD2004/m3 production cost). SEC is per t WATER EXTRACTED (derived from printed SMER, or Table 1 energy over the printed 1935 L water label), not per m3 lumber: no lumber volume per cycle is printed. Measures: fuel and energy-cost savings versus conventional kilns. Other-values: Table 1 per-cycle energies (incl. conventional natural-gas test 4CONV, which has no per-unit basis), Table 2 per-test COP/SMER, energy shares, CO2 potential. Not extracted: wastewater treatment costs (UV peroxidation 68,500 USD, natural mitigation 123,000 USD for 15 m3/day; out of scope). No heat pump capex is printed (only "higher initial capital costs"); no payback figure is printed. The RTC heat-pump brief (rtc_2022_001) and rtc_2023_001 p.135 reprint the COP 3-4.6 and 57% fuel saving from this article.

(1) Text p.8 gives SMER 1.46-2.52 kg/kWh, the conclusion p.10 gives 1.5-2.35 kg/kWh. (2) Hybrid energy-cost saving is 23% on p.6 but 21.5% in the conclusion. (3) Table 1 back-up energy (NG) is called both steam coil energy and natural gas consumption.
